metadata.goal: Analyze the provided trajectory histories to compare observed mode composition, repeated spatial use, and driving-speed behaviour across three users.
metadata.dataset_description: A point-level derived WorldTrace case containing 18 trajectories from three named users in South Brooklyn. The CSV exposes timestamps, coordinates, mode, and point-level speed.

insight_list.insight: Within the provided histories, user_01 and user_02 prefer driving rather than walking, while user_03 has no obvious preference because the observed car and walking counts are balanced.

plot.title: Observed Movement Modes by User
plot.description: Counts of the provided car and walking trajectories for each user. The legend is placed below the bars so it does not cover user_03.

insight_list.question: How are the observed driving and walking trips distributed across the three user histories?
insight_list.actionable_insight: The provided histories support car-dominant labels for user_01 and user_02, but not for user_03; this conclusion is based on the observed trip counts only.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
summary = df.drop_duplicates('trajectory_id')
counts = summary.groupby(['user_id', 'travel_mode']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
ax = counts.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True)
ax.set_title('Observed Movement Modes by User')
ax.set_xlabel('User')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of trajectories')
ax.legend(title='Movement mode', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 0.80, 1))

insight_list.insight: Across all provided driving trajectories, the three users pass through the same South Brooklyn area and their paths overlap along the same road corridor; the walking paths are shown separately rather than being used to support the driving-road claim.

plot.title: Driving and Walking Trajectories in the Same Local Area
plot.description: Two separate geographic maps: one for all driving trajectories and one for all walking trajectories, each tightly cropped to its mode and drawn over real OpenStreetMap road geometries as a sharp vector basemap.

insight_list.question: Do the three users repeatedly use the same local area and road corridor when driving?
insight_list.actionable_insight: The driving map provides direct spatial evidence for a shared corridor; the walking map is a separate comparison and should not be conflated with the driving-road conclusion.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
for mode, color in [('car', 'tab:blue'), ('walking', 'tab:green')]:
 subset = df[df['travel_mode'] == mode]
 fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
 for (user, tid), trip in subset.groupby(['user_id', 'trajectory_id']):
 ax.plot(trip['longitude'], trip['latitude'], color=color, linewidth=1.8, alpha=.65)
 ax.set_title(f'{mode.title()} trajectories')
 ax.set_xlabel('Longitude')
 ax.set_ylabel('Latitude')
 ax.set_aspect('equal', adjustable='box')
 fig.tight_layout()
 plt.show()

insight_list.insight: The three users show clearly different driving-speed behaviour: user_01 drives faster and with larger within-trip speed variation, whereas user_02 and user_03 drive at lower, comparatively stable speeds.

plot.title: Driving Speed Behaviour by User
plot.description: The driving-only speed distributions separate user_01 from the two more stable driving profiles.

insight_list.question: How does driving speed behaviour differ across the three users?
insight_list.actionable_insight: The speed comparison separates user_01's higher and more variable driving profile from the stable lower-speed profiles of user_02 and user_03.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
car = df[df['travel_mode'] == 'car'].drop_duplicates(['trajectory_id', 'point_index'])
car.boxplot(column='speed_kmh', by='user_id', grid=False)
plt.suptitle('')
plt.title('Driving Speed Behaviour by User')
plt.ylabel('Speed (km/h)')
plt.tight_layout()

insights: Within the provided histories, user_01 and user_02 prefer driving rather than walking, while user_03 has no obvious preference because the observed car and walking counts are balanced.

Across all provided driving trajectories, the three users pass through the same South Brooklyn area and their paths overlap along the same road corridor; the walking paths are shown separately rather than being used to support the driving-road claim.

The three users show clearly different driving-speed behaviour: user_01 drives faster and with larger within-trip speed variation, whereas user_02 and user_03 drive at lower, comparatively stable speeds.
summary: Within the provided histories, user_01 and user_02 prefer driving rather than walking while user_03 has no obvious preference. Across all provided driving trajectories, the three users pass through the same local South Brooklyn area and shared road corridor. Their driving speeds separate into a higher, more variable profile for user_01 versus stable lower-speed profiles for user_02 and user_03.
